key_insight: A rollout-based world model lets you optimize music recommendations for listeners' emotional states using only offline data, enabling safe policy improvement without risky live experiments on vulnerable clinical users.
problem_solved: How to learn and deploy music recommendation policies that reliably shape affective outcomes when online experimentation is ethically or practically impossible (e.g., clinical populations who cannot easily skip tracks or report distress).
method: Learn a predictive world model of user affect from offline listening and passive/clinical signals.
Perform rollout-based policy evaluation and optimization inside the learned model to search for preference-aware, affective policies offline.
Integrate safety constraints and affect-preference objectives to avoid distressing recommendations while maximizing therapeutic or wellness outcomes.
impact: Enables practitioners to build and validate affect-aware recommender policies in sensitive domains using model-based offline optimization, bridging recommender systems, offline RL, and health-safe AI. This approach reduces ethical risk and accelerates deployment in real-world clinical settings.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: offline data → world model → simulated rollouts → policy optimizer → deployed recommender

paper_title: Affective Music Recommendation: A Rollout-Based World Model for Offline Preference Optimization
paper_authors: Audrey Chan, Aaron Labbé, Jacob Lavoie, Jordan Bannister, Arsène Fansi Tchango
